full_judgment:
7. It is decided in the case of Albert David (Bangladesh) Ltd. VS. M/S Nedlloyd Lijnen B.V. Rotterdam 34 DLR (1982) 356 that this court as the Court of Admiralty exercises the same jurisdiction as the High Court of England exercised in 1890 under the Admiralty Court Act of 1861. The plaintiff has invoked sections 6 and 5 of that Act of 1861. 

 9. Mr. M. Hafizullah has cited Palmer V. Zarifi Brothers 3 ASP (New series) MLC 540 in support of his contention that the Plaintiff's suit is maintainable in this Court in its Admiralty Jurisdiction. The reported case does not appear to be one under the Admiralty Court Act 1861. Besides, in that case there was evidence that the defendants undertook to pay for any unreasonable delay and they took delivery under the provisions of the bill of lading which contained the following condition: 

 10. As the instant suit is not for damages done to the goods or any part thereof or for any breach of duty or breach of the contract on the part of the owner, master or crew of the Ship the present case does not come within section 6. Finding it difficult to bring the case within section 6 it has been urged that the suit will not fail wholly and the plaintiff's claim for incidental charges amounting to Tk. 75.000/- is within the Admiralty jurisdiction of this Court under section 5 of the Court of Admiralty Act, 1861. 

 14. In the instant case nor attempt has been made to show that the claimed incidental expenses were necessaries to the ship. Mere assertion at the time of the hearing of the matter will be of no avail to the Plaintiff when no such case is eithers made out in the plaint and proved before the Court. In claiming payment for supplying necessaries to a ship it is not required that the term 'necessaries' must be written in the plaint, but there must be clear averments from which the Court can come to a finding that the expenses incurred were for supply of necessaries to the ship. As there are no such averments in the plaint nor there is evidence in this regard I hold that this suit is not for any claim for necessaries supplied to the vessel in question and hence it does not come within the purview of section 5 of the Admiralty Court Act, 1861.
